core_technique: Anti-diagonal (wavefront) Needleman-Wunsch DP over d = i+j with three rotating O(n) diagonal buffers, a reversed copy of b for unit-stride access, and `#pragma omp simd` vectorization of the independent cells within each diagonal.

Standard Needleman-Wunsch global alignment DP computed in anti-diagonal wavefront order with three rolling O(n) diagonal buffers (b pre-reversed for unit-stride, auto-vectorizable inner loops), plus a two-row row-major DP fallback for n < 64.
Full O(n^2) Needleman-Wunsch DP evaluated in anti-diagonal (wavefront) order with three rolling diagonal buffers and one sequence reversed so each diagonal is a contiguous SIMD-vectorizable loop
Full Needleman-Wunsch global alignment DP computed on anti-diagonal wavefronts with three rolling score vectors and an AVX2 SIMD inner loop (reversed b for contiguous loads).

Full O(n^2) Needleman-Wunsch DP (with a scalar fallback for n<64), computed on anti-diagonal wavefronts with three rolling buffers and AVX2 32-bit SIMD max/blend — the standard aligner plus a generic wavefront-vectorisation optimisation, with no enumeration of single-gap shifts, no per-trial mismatch tally, and no minimum-over-trials selection.
xxHash64 verbatim: four independent multiply-rotate-add accumulator lanes over 32-byte stripes, lane merge, length-mixed tail processing, and an xor-shift/multiply avalanche finalizer.

Jenkins one-at-a-time style hash: a single 64-bit accumulator seeded with len, per byte doing h += data[i]; h += h<<20; h ^= h>>12 (shift-add-xor self-feedback), plus a three-step shift-add/xor final avalanche — i.e. the standard one-accumulator shift-xor-fold family that FNV-1a/xxHash belong to, so the native's mechanism survives only because it coincides with the known way.

Bob Jenkins one-at-a-time hash widened to 64 bits: per-byte add plus a fixed add-shift/xor-shift mixing pair on a single accumulator, followed by a three-step shift/xor/add finalizer — no multiplication, so not FNV/xxHash multiply-based mixing.

xxHash64: four interleaved 64-bit accumulator lanes over 32-byte blocks with multiply/rotate-left-31/multiply rounds, rotate-and-add lane merge, 8-byte and 1-byte tail folding, and a MurmurHash3 fmix64 avalanche finalizer (with a single-accumulator FNV-1a-style path for len < 32).
FNV-1a byte-wise xor-multiply accumulation (8x unrolled, serial dependency chain) followed by the MurmurHash3 fmix64 finalizer.

Dijkstra's single-source shortest path over a CSR graph, with a static cost-model dispatch between an O(n²+m) array-scan min-extraction variant (with an optional OpenMP min-reduction) and a standard binary-heap O((n+m)log n) variant.

Textbook Dijkstra on a CSR graph: O(n^2) linear array scan for the minimum tentative distance (a value-only vectorizable reduction plus an index-recovery pass) for small or dense graphs, switching to a standard binary-heap Dijkstra for large sparse graphs.

Round-synchronous pull-based Bellman-Ford over a reverse-CSR graph with double-buffered dist arrays, per-node min-reduction each round, an active/changed frontier flag to skip unchanged sources, and OpenMP parallelism — with a guarded escape to binary-heap Dijkstra only for sparse/large (n>4000 and avg degree<8) inputs.

Dijkstra SSSP with a CSR build and a size/density guard: plain O(n^2) array-scan Dijkstra for small or dense graphs, else sequential delta-stepping with distance-indexed buckets and a light/heavy edge partition (delta = mean edge weight)

Dijkstra's algorithm over CSR adjacency with a dense O(n^2) linear-scan minimum selection plus array relaxation, switched by a size/density heuristic to a standard binary-heap Dijkstra for large sparse graphs.

Anti-diagonal (i+j) wavefront Needleman-Wunsch with AVX2 SIMD across each diagonal, three rotating O(n) diagonal buffers, plus a score-bound-derived band clamped to be non-binding and a scalar row-DP fallback.

Exact Needleman-Wunsch computed as an anti-diagonal (wavefront) DP with three rolling diagonal buffers, one sequence pre-reversed so both reads run forward for AVX2/AVX-512 16-bit max/add vectorisation, restricted to a provably safe band W = floor(2H/5) from an O(n) Hamming-distance prepass, with a scalar rolling-row NW fallback for small n or allocation failure.

Exact banded Needleman-Wunsch (two rows, AVX2 prefix-max/Hillis-Steele gap scan) whose band width is derived from lower bounds — SIMD Hamming score plus an O(n) one-gap probe — with a self-certifying narrow pass; the banded DP, not the native scheme, produces the returned score.

Exact banded anti-diagonal (wavefront) Needleman-Wunsch with AVX2 SIMD, where the band half-width is derived from a score lower bound obtained by scanning the ungapped and all single-shift alignments; plain two-row DP fallback for small n.

Banded anti-diagonal SIMD (AVX2) Needleman-Wunsch wavefront over int16/int32 lanes, with the band half-width W derived from a single-shift Hamming-based score lower bound (plus an exact two-row DP fallback for small n or allocation failure).

xxHash64: four independent 64-bit lanes over 32-byte blocks using add-multiply-rotl(31)-multiply rounds, a rotate-and-sum lane merge with mergeRound steps, length injection, 8/4/1-byte tail processing, and a MurmurHash3-style xor-shift/multiply final avalanche — all rotation amounts and constants fixed, with no data-dependent fold angle and no cross-lane agreement or refold-until-consistent step.

xxHash64: four 64-bit lanes fed 8-byte words with the add-multiply/rotl-31/multiply round, lane merge by rotate-and-add, 8/4/1-byte tail folds, plus an xor-shift-multiply avalanche finalizer — with a small added triangular cross-lane carry (each lane XORs the rotated previous lane's round output, plus a 'callus' word persisting across iterations) as the only non-standard element.

SipHash-2-4 with a zero key: one 256-bit four-word state, each 8-byte little-endian word XOR-absorbed and mixed by a fixed 2 SipRound ARX (add/rotate/xor, no multiply) permutations, length byte in the tail word, 4 finalization rounds, folded to one 64-bit word — plus a non-standard 32-byte-per-2-rounds wide fast path.

Sponge-style absorbing hash over a 16x64-bit (4x4) state: each 64-byte block is XOR-ed into the rate lanes, then permuted by 4 double-rounds of the BLAKE2b G function applied column-wise (add/xor/rotate-32,24,16,63) interleaved with an AES-like ShiftRows lane rotation, followed by a 12-layer finalisation permutation and an XOR-rotate fold to 64 bits — with a separate splitmix64/xxHash-class multiply-xor-shift accumulator only for buffers under 64 bytes.

Serial single-accumulator absorb built on chained CRC-32C steps (hardware _mm_crc32_u64 with a table-driven fallback), each step seeded by the running accumulator and combined with a rotate-xor side path to preserve the bits CRC truncates, followed by a splitmix64/degski-style 7-operation xor-shift/multiply finalizer.

Dijkstra SSSP over directed CSR using a compacted tentative-distance frontier array with SIMD (AVX2/AVX-512) linear argmin extract-min, position back-index for decrease-key, and a lazy binary-heap Dijkstra fallback once a work budget is exceeded — i.e. the textbook array-scan/heap Dijkstra pair with generic vectorisation.

Dijkstra over a compacted live frontier whose minimum is found by an AVX2-vectorized linear argmin scan (with index recovery pass), plus a permanent-settled flag array, CSR edge build, out-degree-zero pruning, and a 4-ary lazy-deletion heap fallback once the frontier exceeds a density-tuned threshold — i.e. the well-known array-scan Dijkstra variant with SIMD, backed by heap Dijkstra.

Frontier-based synchronized Bellman-Ford over CSR: dist held read-only for a whole round while per-node candidate minima accumulate (strict nd < dist && nd < cand test, SIMD gather-assisted), then all candidates committed at once and only changed nodes form the next frontier — hedged by an O(n^2) SIMD array-scan Dijkstra for dense/tiny graphs and a work-budget bailout to binary-heap Dijkstra.

Delta-stepping SSSP: CSR with light/heavy edge partition and a power-of-two ring of distance buckets (a monotone bucket priority queue, i.e. Dial-style Dijkstra with in-bucket relaxation to a fixpoint), plus an explicit branch to plain O(n^2) array-scan Dijkstra (AVX-vectorised min-scan) for dense or small graphs.

Standard non-negative single-source Dijkstra over a CSR adjacency built by counting sort, with a cost-model switch between an O(n^2)-style linear (AVX2) minimum scan over a compacted frontier array and a 4-ary binary heap with lazy-deletion, plus a mid-run escape hatch from scan mode to heap mode.

Anti-diagonal (wavefront) Needleman-Wunsch: cells of constant i+j computed as one SIMD-vectorized diagonal from the two previous diagonals in rotating O(n) buffers, with b stored reversed for unit-stride access and int16/int32 width regimes plus a scalar small-n path

Standard Needleman-Wunsch global-alignment DP computed on anti-diagonal wavefronts with three rolling score buffers and AVX2 int16 SIMD (with scalar int32 anti-diagonal and two-row scalar fallbacks) — a textbook vectorisation, single forward pass, no revisiting and gaps cost -2, not zero.

Exact Needleman-Wunsch computed as a score-bound banded anti-diagonal wavefront with 16-bit SSE2/AVX2 lanes (plus scalar two-row DP fallbacks), band width derived from the identity-diagonal match count

Banded Needleman-Wunsch global alignment (two rolling rows, AVX2 max-plus prefix-scan for the left-gap dependency) with band half-width K=(n-LB)/5 derived from an O(n) lower bound — the diagonal score plus the best single-gap-pair (one-slip) score — and iterative band widening until the returned score certifies the band; the one-slip/max-of-rows native idea survives only as that cheap lower bound, not as the scoring mechanism.

Banded anti-diagonal SIMD Needleman-Wunsch: an O(n) Hamming/one-gap (Kadane) lower-bound score seeds a score-derived band width D=(n-S)/5, refined by a trial narrow pass, then exact banded wavefront DP in int16/int32 AVX2 produces the answer.

Multiply-xor accumulation where each round's rotation amount is data-dependent (a = ((mark ^ state) & 31) + 16), run over four xxHash-style parallel lanes with distinct odd-prime multipliers, then rotate-summed and passed through a Murmur3 fmix64 finalizer.

Wide (256-bit, 4x64) SIMD/ARX block accumulator — XOR 32-byte block, lane add (carry), rotate, lane permute per block, overlapping last-block tail, plus a separate xor-rotate-multiply path for short inputs and an xxHash/splitmix-style multiply-xor-shift finalizer that folds in the length: i.e. standard xxHash-family accumulator hashing.

Multiplication-free ARX streaming hash: each 8-byte word is added into one 64-bit accumulator which is then rotated by a fixed per-lane constant (add-rotate), with an xor-shift after each 32/8-byte group, finished by a bijective rotate/add/xor-shift + 32-bit-half ARX grind avalanche.

Wide 1024-bit state as a 4x4 grid of 64-bit lanes: each 8-byte word XOR'd into its own positional lane, then per-row rotate-plus-xorshift followed by a 90-degree lane permutation and ChaCha-style add/xor/rotate corner folding (AVX2-vectorised, dual cursors reading from both ends), with a murmur3 fmix64 finalizer — multiplication-free bulk ARX permutation, not single-accumulator multiply-xor folding.

Byte-wise rotate-add accumulation (single chain under 64 bytes, seven interleaved parallel lanes above it, xxHash-style) combined at the end and run through a MurmurHash3/SplitMix-style multiply-xorshift fmix64 finalizer extended to seven rounds.

Textbook Dijkstra with two selection strategies: an O(n²) linear argmin scan over a swap-compacted unsettled array (AVX2-vectorised) for small/dense graphs, and a 3-ary heap with decrease-key for large sparse graphs, over CSR-built directed edges.

Dijkstra's algorithm on a CSR graph with a work-estimate switch between an O(n^2) SIMD (AVX2) two-pass linear argmin scan over tentative distances (dense case, dead-end vertices permuted out of the scanned prefix) and a lazy 4-ary binary-heap Dijkstra (sparse case).

CSR build, then round-synchronous frontier Bellman-Ford (stamped active set) with a work budget that hands over to binary-heap Dijkstra, plus a dense/small-n branch that is plain O(n^2) array-scan Dijkstra with an AVX2 argmin.

Bucket/time-wheel (Dial's–delta-stepping style) label-correcting shortest paths: arrival times quantised by delta into a circular array of NB tick buckets drained in time order, with immediate re-emission on improvement, stale-entry skipping via qs[]/dist[] checks, plus a guarded dense/small-n O(n^2) array-scan Dijkstra fast path.

Dijkstra on a CSR graph with a size/density heuristic switching between a two-level blocked SIMD (AVX2) array-scan min-selection with NaN sentinels for settled nodes (the O(n·sqrt(n))-ish dense variant of the classic O(n^2) array scan) and a 4-ary binary-heap Dijkstra for sparse graphs — both standard textbook techniques, with an OpenMP parallel CSR build.

Anti-diagonal (wavefront) Needleman-Wunsch: each anti-diagonal d = i+j is computed as one vector pass from the two previous anti-diagonals held in three rotating buffers, with one sequence pre-reversed so the diagonal becomes a contiguous SIMD-friendly stride-1 span, vectorised with AVX2/AVX-512BW 16-bit lanes (32-bit variant past the 16-bit score range, scalar two-row DP only for n < 32).

Standard Needleman-Wunsch global alignment computed as an AVX2 anti-diagonal (wavefront) vectorized DP over three rolling diagonals, with int16/int32 width selection by sequence length and a scalar rolling-row DP fallback.

Banded Needleman-Wunsch computed as a SIMD anti-diagonal wavefront (with b reversed for contiguous diagonal access), band half-width derived from a score lower bound (diagonal identity score plus a w=8 probe), plus a rolling-row exact NW fallback for small n.

Exact Needleman-Wunsch computed as an anti-diagonal wavefront DP restricted to a certified band w=(n-L)/5 (L from a cheap O(n) match-count / single-shift lower bound), with an int16 AVX2 kernel and a plain rolling-row DP for short inputs — i.e. a banded SIMD DP (KSW2/SSW-style) rather than the native's counting scheme.

O(n) enumeration of all single-gap-shift alignments (Hamming prefix-mismatch arrays D/F with a running-minimum scan over gap positions, both shift directions) to get the exact best one-gap score, which is then used as a lower bound to prove a band width W=(n-best)/5 — returning directly when W<=1, otherwise running banded DP (AVX2 int16 anti-diagonal or scalar int32) only as a bounded-width fallback for high-divergence inputs.

xxHash64-style multi-accumulator streaming hash: four 64-bit lanes folded over 64-byte blocks with fixed-constant xor-rotate-add steps, then merged and finalized by a MurmurHash3-style xor-shift/multiply avalanche including the length.

A persistent 8x64-bit accumulator state (seeded with fixed constants plus the length) that absorbs input blocks by XOR into the already-permuted state and then applies BLAKE2b-style ARX quarter-round permutations with alternating column/diagonal lane pairings, followed by input-free finalization rounds folding the eight lanes down to one 64-bit word; no multiply-xor-shift (FNV/xxHash) accumulator is used.

Single 64-bit accumulator folded over the buffer with multiply-free XOR-of-rotations mixing in which one rotation amount is re-derived from the state each round (self-feeding data-dependent rotate), fixed rounds per chunk, an AVX2 4-lane variant joined by a cross-lane XOR-permutation bijection, and a 5-round rotate/xorshift finalizer keyed with the length.

ChaCha-style ARX permutation (add/rotate/xor quarter-rounds, multiplication-free, plus extra xorshifts) over a 16x64-bit state absorbing 128-byte blocks by XOR with column rounds then diagonal rounds, block counter and length injected, finished by a halving tree-fold and xorshift-add finalizer to 64 bits (4x4-word small-state variant for len<128).

Multi-lane (8-way scalar / 16-way AVX2) rotate-add byte accumulation with length tempering, folded into one word and finished by a 6-step halving xor-shift + rotate ladder plus one shift-add — i.e. an xxHash-style multi-accumulator hash with a standard strong finalizer; the native's single unbroken chain survives only on the <32-byte path, and the seven-organ halving ladder survives fully but only as the final mix.

Standard non-negative single-source Dijkstra over a CSR adjacency, with a two-regime priority queue: SIMD (AVX2) linear argmin scan over a compact frontier array while the frontier is small (<=2048), then a one-time switch to a 3-ary indexed min-heap with true decrease-key, plus software prefetching of relaxation targets.

Dijkstra's algorithm with a compacted frontier array and AVX2-vectorised linear extract-min scan (the classic O(n^2)-style array-scan variant), adaptively switching to a binary-heap Dijkstra mid-run when measured scan cost exceeds a degree/log-n threshold; CSR edge layout and a Bellman-Ford fallback on allocation failure.

Frontier-guided pull-based Bellman-Ford: each round recomputes min over incoming edges of D[src]+w for whole 4-node chunks, via an ELL/4-lane-interleaved reverse adjacency with AVX2 gather + _mm256_min_pd (scalar 4-accumulator reverse-CSR otherwise), with a mu+wmin threshold sweep to settle nodes and a work budget that bails out to binary-heap Dijkstra.

Bucketed/calendar-queue Dijkstra (Dial / delta-stepping style): relaxed vertices are parked in a power-of-two circular bucket array at index floor(dist/delta) and a monotone clock drains each bucket to fixpoint, with heap Dijkstra and an O(n^2) dense scan kept only as guarded fallbacks for small n, skewed weights, or a scan-count abort.

Dijkstra's SSSP on a CSR graph with a size/density regime switch: a blocked (32-wide) array extract-min using cached per-block minima with AVX2 argmin for dense/small graphs, and a 4-ary binary min-heap with lazy deletion otherwise.
